newsitem.title: UK: UK's Camelot to appeal in 49's case.
newsitem.headline: UK's Camelot to appeal in 49's case.

text.p: UK national lottery operator Camelot Group Plc will appeal after a court on Monday dismissed attempts to have a numbers game run by bookmakers declared illegal.

"There needs to be clarification on what constitutes a lottery," a Camelot spokeswoman said, confirming the plans for an appeal. "We want to protect the money raised for good causes by the national lottery."
A London magistrate had earlier dismissed Camelot's attempts to outlaw the 49's numbers bet, run by bookmakers Coral, Ladbrokes and William Hill.
The appeal is likely to be heard in a divisional court before judges drawn from Britain's high court. Costs were awarded against Camelot in Monday's case.
49's chairman John Brown had earlier urged Camelot to drop the action against the game, which has now survived a series of challenges to its legality.

"49's has been of some help to the bookmaking industry in helping us to reduce the damage done to our business by the lottery - we have lost 3,000 jobs and closed 600 shops since the lottery started," Brown said in a statement.

Chris Bell, managing director of Ladbroke's Racing, told Reuters that numbers betting, including bets on the Irish national lottery, raised some 200 million stg in annual turnover for UK bookmakers. But he noted that 80 percent of this was paid out in prices.
